name: Karnak Temple
subtitle: Precinct of Amun-Ra and Open Air Museum, Luxor

hours.note: Daily 06:00–17:00 (Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, checked November 2026). Ramadan 2027 is expected to end about 9 March 2027; hours are sometimes shorter during Ramadan.

eras.name: Middle Kingdom beginnings
eras.summary: A local god, Amun, gets his first stone temple under Senusret I.

eras.name: Early New Kingdom
eras.summary: Theban kings drive out the Hyksos; Thutmose I builds pylons and obelisks.

eras.name: Hatshepsut and Thutmose III
eras.summary: Obelisks, the Red Chapel, the Akhmenu: Karnak becomes the empire's great temple.

eras.name: Amenhotep III to Horemheb
eras.summary: Amenhotep III builds big; Akhenaten turns against Amun; Tutankhamun and Horemheb restore him.

eras.name: Ramesside kings
eras.summary: The Great Hypostyle Hall, battle reliefs, and the temples of Ramesses III and Khonsu.

eras.name: Priest-kings and Libyan pharaohs
eras.summary: The High Priests of Amun rule Thebes; Shoshenq I records his campaign.

eras.name: Kushites, Saites and the last native kings
eras.summary: Taharqa's kiosk, the Assyrian sack of Thebes, Nectanebo's walls and the unfinished First Pylon.

eras.name: Greek and Roman Egypt
eras.summary: Alexander's successors rebuild the sanctuary; Rome takes an obelisk; the temple closes.

eras.name: Rediscovery and conservation
eras.summary: Churches and a village in the ruins, then travellers, excavation, collapse and restoration.

stops.name: Car and coach park
stops.look: The car, taxi and coach park on the north side of the visitor centre, off the Corniche road.
stops.note: Taxis and tour coaches drop off here. Agree a pick-up point with the driver before you go in.

stops.name: Visitor centre
stops.look: The visitor centre, with a large model of the temple and toilets (a small fee is usual).
stops.note: Last proper toilets until the ones by the Open Air Museum and the Sacred Lake. Fill water bottles before going on.

stops.name: Security check and entrance
stops.look: Security and ticket check on the walk from the visitor centre to the temple, about 200 m before the quay.
stops.note: Tickets are reported to be card-only. Keep the ticket: it is checked again at the Open Air Museum.

stops.name: Karnak in brief
stops.look: The whole story in a few points, to put every stop in context. Also on the Timeline tab any time.

stops.name: Quay and tribune
stops.dateLabel: Ramesside (the obelisk of Sety II, about 1200–1194 BC)
stops.look: The stone platform at the western end of the temple, where boats once moored; the small obelisk is Sety II's.
stops.note: Open ground, no shade.

stops.name: Avenue of ram-headed sphinxes
stops.dateLabel: set out about 1279–1213 BC, rams re-inscribed later
stops.look: The double row of ram-headed sphinxes leading to the First Pylon; each holds a small figure of the king between its front paws.
stops.note: Usually busy with groups between 09:00 and 11:00.

stops.name: The First Pylon
stops.look: The great gateway, 113 m wide, seen from the rams. Its stone faces were never dressed smooth.

stops.name: Builders' ramp behind the First Pylon
stops.look: Once through the pylon, turn right: the mud-brick slope against the back of the south tower is what is left of the builders' ramp.

stops.name: Triple shrine of Sety II
stops.look: The small three-roomed shrine on the left (north) side of the forecourt, for the boats of Amun, Mut and Khonsu.
stops.note: The site board calls these the "Chapels of Sety I"; the scholarly sources give Sety II.

stops.name: Kiosk of Taharqa
stops.look: The single tall papyrus column standing alone in the middle of the forecourt, the last of ten.

stops.name: Temple of Ramesses III
stops.look: The complete small temple cutting into the right (south) side of the forecourt, with statues of the king as Osiris lining its court.
stops.note: Partly shaded inside.

stops.name: Bubastite Portal
stops.look: The gateway in the south-east corner of the forecourt; on the wall beside it Shoshenq I smites his enemies above rows of name-rings for captured towns.

stops.name: Second Pylon and colossus
stops.look: The pink granite colossus of a king with a small princess at his feet, beside the doorway into the Hypostyle Hall.

stops.name: Great Hypostyle Hall
stops.look: 134 giant columns; walk the central aisle first, then look up at the stone window grilles high on the sides.
stops.note: Good shade. Busiest place on the site.

stops.name: Battle reliefs of Sety I
stops.look: Outside the north wall of the Hypostyle Hall: Sety I in his chariot charging through his enemies, carved across the whole wall.
stops.note: Leave the hall by the north door. Morning light rakes across the carving.

stops.name: Obelisks of Thutmose I and Hatshepsut
stops.look: Two standing obelisks: Thutmose I's just beyond the Third Pylon, and his daughter Hatshepsut's, the taller, rising out of the hall behind the Fourth Pylon.

stops.name: Granite sanctuary
stops.dateLabel: about 323–317 BC, on a site used since the Middle Kingdom
stops.look: The granite shrine where Amun's boat was kept, built in the name of Philip Arrhidaeus; in front stand two granite pillars carved with the lotus and the papyrus.

stops.name: Middle Kingdom court
stops.look: The open, empty-looking court behind the sanctuary; only the granite door sills of Senusret I's temple remain, at the heart of the oldest part of Karnak.
stops.note: Easy to walk straight past.

stops.name: Festival Hall of Thutmose III (Akhmenu)
stops.look: The hall with tent-pole columns, then the small "botanical garden" room carved with plants and animals from the Syrian campaign.
stops.note: Some rooms may be roped off.

stops.name: Temple of Ptah
stops.dateLabel: about 1479–1425 BC, gates added up to the Ptolemies
stops.look: The small temple against the north wall, entered through a series of gates; in the dark right-hand room a black statue of the lioness goddess Sekhmet is lit only from a hole in the roof.
stops.note: A guardian may open the door for a tip.

stops.name: White Chapel of Senusret I (Open Air Museum)
stops.look: The small white limestone pavilion on a raised base, rebuilt from blocks found inside the Third Pylon. Steps on both sides.
stops.note: In the Open Air Museum, north of the forecourt; the ticket is checked again at its gate.

stops.name: Red Chapel of Hatshepsut (Open Air Museum)
stops.look: The long red quartzite and black granite shrine rebuilt from blocks; look for Hatshepsut's chiselled-out figures.
stops.note: In the Open Air Museum.

stops.name: Cachette Court and Seventh Pylon
stops.look: The court south of the Hypostyle Hall where about 750 statues were found buried; beyond it the Seventh Pylon with Thutmose III smiting his enemies.
stops.note: Access to the southern pylons varies; the court is reached from the south side of the Hypostyle Hall.

stops.name: Sacred Lake
stops.dateLabel: New Kingdom, lined in its present form later
stops.look: The great stone-lined pool, about 120 by 77 m, where the priests took water for the rituals and purified themselves.
stops.note: Café on its north-west side.

stops.name: Giant scarab and fallen obelisk
stops.look: The big stone scarab beetle on a pedestal at the corner of the lake; near it lies the broken top of Hatshepsut's second obelisk.
stops.note: Visitors walk round the scarab for luck; a modern custom.

stops.name: View across the Sacred Lake
stops.look: From the south-east corner of the lake, point the camera north-west: the water in front, with the obelisks and the Hypostyle Hall behind.
stops.note: Little shade.

stops.name: Southern pylons (Eighth to Tenth)
stops.dateLabel: about 1473 BC (Eighth Pylon) to about 1323–1295 BC (Ninth and Tenth)
stops.look: The line of gateways running south from the Cachette Court towards the Temple of Mut; the Eighth, built for Hatshepsut, is the oldest pylon still standing at Karnak.
stops.note: Access to the southern axis has varied; visitors photographed the Eighth and Ninth Pylons in 2025.

stops.name: Temple of Khonsu
stops.look: The complete temple of the moon god in the south-west corner, entered through a pylon; the Temple of Opet is beside it.
stops.note: Quieter than the main axis. Steps at the entrance; may be closed or partly closed.

stops.name: Temple of the Hearing Ear and the eastern gate
stops.dateLabel: about 1279–1213 BC; the obelisk stood here from about 1400 BC to AD 357
stops.look: Behind the Akhmenu: the small temple where ordinary people could pray to Amun, on the spot where the obelisk now in Rome (the Lateran obelisk) once stood; the Nectanebo gate is beyond.
stops.note: At the far eastern end; usually very quiet.

stops.name: Toilets by the Open Air Museum
stops.look: Toilets on the north side of the forecourt, on the way to the Open Air Museum.
stops.note: Small fee usual.

stops.name: Café by the Sacred Lake
stops.look: Small café with seats in the shade on the north-west side of the Sacred Lake.

stops.name: Toilets east of the Sacred Lake
stops.look: Toilet block east of the Sacred Lake.
stops.note: Small fee usual.
